column7: Haworth is situated near the rims of the ancient Haworth and Cabeus craters. The region contains rugged highland terrain and nearby permanently shadowed regions.
column8: Wueller et al. identify HW10 as a candidate from which permanently shadowed regions below 110 K are accessible. Such regions are valuable for studying the thermal environment and potentially sampling lunar volatiles.
column9: The study's prose describes extended Sun and Earth visibility for HW10, but its Table A2 reports much shorter maximum consecutive Sun-and-Earth visibility intervals during the specified midsummers. Do not use a >25-day continuous midsummer claim without reconciling this difference. Small hazards may also be unresolved in the 20 m/pixel DEM.

column7: Mons Malapert is an approximately 6 km high massif, interpreted as a remnant rim of the South Pole–Aitken basin. MMA04 is located on its southern base; the wider region contains a ridge, southern flank, and nearby shadowed craters.
column8: The 2026 study identifies MMA04 as the most promising point in this region for volatile exploration. Permanently shadowed regions below 125 K are accessible within approximately 2 km. The study reports limited but adequate illumination for a 6.5-day surface mission during selected midsummers.
column9: Illumination is seasonal and not continuous across every modeled year. The NASA notional summit coordinate (-85.964°, 357.681°) is a different point; Kring et al. found it did not satisfy the baseline HLS landing constraints under their assessment. The selected MMA04 point must not be confused with that notional coordinate.

column7: Nobile Rim 1 lies on Mons Mouton near the western rim of Nobile crater. The region contains elevated crater-rim terrain and nearby shadowed terrain.
column8: Wueller et al. identify NR101 as one of the most consistently illuminated candidate points in Nobile Rim 1. Their model indicates more than 17 consecutive sunlit days during every modeled midsummer through 2032. This supports longer surface operations and exploration planning.
column9: The illumination result is model-dependent and applies to the study's modeled midsummer periods. It is not a guarantee of illumination for all dates. The region should not be assumed to contain the coldest or most volatile-rich PSRs solely from this result.
